The analyst's core answer holds up. A full-HTTPS build needs only data patches: keep the existing discovery-host patch at 0x232711F, replace the embedded Go Daddy Class 2 root PEM at 0x2318F2F (1446-byte slot, strlen-terminated) with our own root, NUL-padded, and apply none of the 7 https-to-http FIXED_PATCHES.

I re-checked every patch byte, the BFCertificateProvider code, configureCURL, curl's step1 (it never loads default CAs, sends SNI via SSL_ctrl 55, and runs the callback after SSL_CTX_set_verify), and the claim that nothing else references the slot (code, relocations and raw pointers; register-tracked scan). All of it is confirmed. The prototype changes only bytes inside the slot and host ranges. A fresh test root (644 bytes) read back out of a patched library verifies a SAN=api.example.com leaf over TLS 1.2 (ECDHE-ECDSA, ecdsa_secp256r1_sha256).

Corrections:
(1) **Purchase requests still use plain HTTP.** CommonUtils::getPurchasePhpUrl, used by GameScene::accessPurchasePhp from the ShopBuyCoin*, BundlePurchaseInfoStartScene and MultiGachaIapPurchaseInfoStartScene scenes, builds "http://" + PURCHASE_URL() + "/" from the separate "http://" literal at 0x23270B0. PURCHASE_URL() resolves the same "game" endpoint as PHP_URL(), so the HTTPS build still sends shop and purchase requests to http://api.example.com. Either keep the Caddy http site permanently, or apply a new, verified 2-instruction patch (P4) at 0x1CE93D0/0x1CE93D4 that points it at the "https://" literal.
(2) **"Only two readers of host[1]" is wrong.** NM+0x48 (host[1]) is also read by NetworkManager::WebviewNewsURL, WebviewDailyBonusURL, WebviewGachaBannerURL and WebviewSocialURL. None of these has a caller (no bl/b, no relocation), so host[1] is still effectively dead and the conclusion stands.
(3) **Expected ciphers and PEM size.** The expected cipher set must include ECDHE-ECDSA-CHACHA20-POLY1305 (52393). The local emulation negotiated AES256-GCM. A root PEM is about 635–650 bytes, not exactly 635.
(4) **TLS-failure behaviour is known.** The verified boot notes (android_boot_re.json) say a transport or TLS failure fires no callback and retries every 30 s, so the client stays stuck on the title screen.
(5) **Address fix.** NetworkManager::sharedInstance starts at 0xF5C224; 0xF5C2B8 is its call to BFCertificateProvider::shared().

Prototype re/work/https/out/libgame.so differs from the original in 1407 bytes, all within 0x2318f2f..0x23194d4 or 0x232711f..0x2327132. Its extracted PEM is 635 B and verifies the test leaf.

Fresh re-run (re/work/https-verify/pki, TEST ONLY keys) with the exact PKI commands from the spec under OpenSSL 3.6.2. -not_before and -not_after work on req -x509 and x509 -req. The root PEM is 644 B. patch_https_proto.py wrote 644 B PEM + 802 NUL, and 0x23194d4.. still reads '\0 9PWWebView\0'. The PEM was extracted from the patched lib. s_server -tls1_2 and s_client -tls1_2 with the curl default cipher string, groups X25519:P-256:P-521:P-384 and -CAfile extracted PEM gave TLSv1.2, ECDHE-ECDSA-AES256-GCM-SHA384, ecdsa_secp256r1_sha256 and Verify return code 0.
inferred: A shorter PEM followed by NUL padding is safe. The length passed is -1 (strlen), and nothing else in the library refers into the slot. Maximum PEM size is 1445 bytes. The NUL at 0x23194d4 and the bytes at and after 0x23194d5 must not change.

Only one root is ever trusted: PEM_read_bio_X509 runs once and the callback adds only [0x28a8228]. Two P-256 PEMs would fit in the space, but the second would be ignored, so a root change requires a new APK.

If the PEM fails to parse, [0x28a8228] stays NULL and the callback adds nothing. The trust store is then empty and every curl HTTPS request fails (CURLE_SSL_CACERT). Per the verified boot notes, /dls then never calls back and the client retries every 30 s, stuck on the title screen.
The mechanism is proven in practice: the original game used exactly this path (embedded single Go Daddy root, CAINFO/CAPATH NULL, SSL_CTX callback) against Gumi's servers.

Hostname checking follows curl 7.52.1 verifyhost(): dNSName SAN first, CN only when there is no DNS SAN. OpenSSL 1.1.0c verifies with purpose ssl_server. The root needs CA:TRUE and keyCertSign. The leaf should carry EKU serverAuth and KU digitalSignature. Use a plain 'BEGIN CERTIFICATE' header, not 'TRUSTED CERTIFICATE'.

Against Caddy 2.10 (Go crypto/tls, minimum TLS1.2) the result is TLS1.2 (the client has no TLS1.3), ECDHE-ECDSA with AES128-GCM, AES256-GCM or CHACHA20-POLY1305 (IDs 49195, 49196 or 52393), X25519, ecdsa_secp256r1_sha256 and ALPN http/1.1.

Host index 1 (NM+0x48) is never used on a live path. Its only reads are reinitEndPoints, NetworkRequest's indexed lookup (never called with HOST=1) and four uncalled Webview*URL helpers. No patch or server change is needed. If 'servers' is ever sent it must be a JSON object, because jsoncpp non-const operator[] on an array or string asserts.

WITHOUT P4, the HTTPS build still sends shop and IAP-scene requests (accessPurchasePhp) to http://api.example.com/ over plain HTTP through curl. The Caddy http://api.example.com site is therefore needed permanently, not just during the transition, and the test-plan claim 'no api.example.com traffic on :80 from this device' was wrong. WITH P4 (two re-encoded instructions, only in getPurchasePhpUrl) those requests also use https and the pinned root. getResourceUrl, which shares the 0x23270b0 literal, is unaffected because the literal itself is not modified.
The CDN path is unchanged: getResourceUrl ('http://' + RES_URL()) and the Java ch.boye loader. It must stay on http, because neither path trusts the private root.

WebView pages (getPhpUrl-based notice/agreement/FAQ, showTermsAndConditions) and Pusher (Java, system trust store) will not trust the private root. With targetSdk 30 and no NSC they are already blocked as cleartext in the HTTP build, so this is not a regression. A future fix would need a publicly-trusted certificate on a separate host plus code or URL changes.
One /dls reply (scheme-less hosts) serves both APKs, so no game-server change is needed. Do not put a port in public_host.
The leaf has no AIA/OCSP URL, so Caddy will not attempt OCSP stapling for it (no warnings expected).
Installing over the HTTP build with the same package name and signing key keeps UserDefault and SaveData. PT_SERVER_URL is '' after login today, so no stale scheme is carried over.
unknowns: The real OpenSSL 1.1.0c + curl 7.52.1 stack was not run against Caddy 2.10. It was emulated with OpenSSL 3.6.2 restricted to TLS1.2 and the client's cipher string and groups. The emulator test closes this.
curl verifyhost() and the 7.52.1 defaults were taken from upstream source plus the version string; only the step1 call sequence was disassembled.

Whether any code path issues CCHttpClient file-type (processFileTask: no configureCURL, so an empty trust store) downloads to an https URL. NetworkRequestFile has no callers, but other CCHttpRequest file-type users were not traced. Keep file downloads on http.

What the server currently returns for the accessPurchasePhp requests (shop/IAP scenes) and whether those flows are reachable or useful at all (Google Play billing is gone). This affects only how important P4 is, not correctness.
Whether a curl transport/TLS error is surfaced to logcat (error buffer 0x28b6140).

=== 0. RESULT ===
HTTPS build = original v2.19.6 arm64 libgame.so (sha256 076c8ed12e84d122938255c1530a4d4b1853d876b5928dd0c2389538fc4cad95) with these patches:
  (a) Discovery host at 0x232711F: 'api-sl.bfww.gumi.sg\0' (20 B) -> 'api.example.com' + NULs. Same as today.
  (b) Pinned root: our root PEM written over the embedded Go Daddy Class 2 root at 0x2318F2F, NUL-padded through 0x23194D4.
  (c) RECOMMENDED, P4 (new): getPurchasePhpUrl points at 'https://' instead of 'http://'. Two instruction words, see section 3.
Apply NONE of the 7 FIXED_PATCHES (P1 0x2369CE3; P2 0xF5FBEC/0xF5FBF0/0xF5FBF4; P3 0x1C7A5C8/0x1C7A5DC/0x1C7A5E0). The original bytes already build 'https://'.
Server side: Caddy adds an https://api.example.com site using a leaf (SAN DNS:api.example.com) signed by our root. It KEEPS http://api.example.com, which is needed for the legacy APK, and permanently if P4 is not applied. /dls is unchanged. Assets stay on http://cdn.example.com.

=== 1. Pinned-root mechanism (verified) ===
Load (once, on first BFCertificateProvider::shared() @0xF48C34; called from NetworkManager ctor 0xF5C108 and from sharedInstance @0xF5C224 at 0xF5C2B8; both then call CCHttpClient::setCertificateProvider):
- 0xF48CB4: 80 9E 00 90  adrp x0,0x2318000
- 0xF48CB8: 00 BC 3C 91  add x0,x0,#0xF2F
- 0xF48CBC: 01 00 80 12  mov w1,#-1
- 0xF48CC0: bl BIO_new_mem_buf. Negative length means strlen (0x21FF8BC tbnz w1,#31 -> strlen); the BIO is read-only.
- 0xF48CD8: PEM_read_bio_X509(bio, &[0x28A8228], NULL, NULL). Only the first certificate is used.

Per connection: curl step1 calls the SSL_CTX callback 0xF48E1C, which does X509_STORE_add_cert(SSL_CTX_get_cert_store(ctx), [0x28A8228]) and returns 0. This happens after SSL_CTX_set_verify(PEER) (0x1F9F490 -> 0x1F9F4A8). No default CA paths are ever loaded: CAINFO/CAPATH are set NULL in configureCURL and step1 has no set_default_verify_paths.

Slot:
- 0x2318F17..0x2318F2E = '21BFCertificateProvider\0' (do not touch).
- 0x2318F2F..0x23194D3 = PEM (1445 B, ends in LF); 0x23194D4 = NUL.
- 0x23194D5.. = '9PWWebView\0' (do not touch).
- sha256 of the 1446 bytes 0x2318F2F..0x23194D4 = cbfb7dcf86bc532d0f503479109faa03fcc68d6b98ef121252551d365b5b4605.
- No other code, relocation or pointer references the slot.

New PEM rules:
- Length 1..1445 bytes; 7-bit ASCII; no NUL; LF line endings; ends with LF.
- Exactly one '-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----' ... '-----END CERTIFICATE-----' block (never 'TRUSTED CERTIFICATE').
- Self-signed CA:TRUE with keyCertSign.
- An EC P-256 root is about 635-650 B.

TLS facts:
- configureCURL @0x102DBD4 is used by processGetTask and processPostTask only: VERIFYHOST=2, VERIFYPEER=1, CAINFO=NULL, CAPATH=NULL, SSL_CTX_FUNCTION=provider callback.
- No CIPHER_LIST and no SSLVERSION are set, so curl's default cipher string is 'ALL:!EXPORT:!EXPORT40:!EXPORT56:!aNULL:!LOW:!RC4:@STRENGTH'.
- SNI is sent for DNS names (SSL_ctrl 55 @0x1F9F834). ALPN is http/1.1.
- Bundled stack is OpenSSL 1.1.0c (TLS1.2 maximum) with libcurl 7.52.1.
- processFileTask has no SSL setup, so keep file downloads on http.

=== 2. Resulting client URLs (HTTPS build) ===
- /dls: https://api.example.com/dls (host[3] = 'https://' + SERVICE_PHP_URL()).
- After /dls (reinitEndPoints @0x1C7A598, with game='api.example.com' and gumilive='api.example.com/'):
  - host[2] = https://api.example.com
  - host[0] = https://api.example.com/ (guest login, wallet)
- getPhpUrl() = https://api.example.com/ (game API via accessPhp).
- getPurchasePhpUrl() (shop/IAP scenes):
  - without P4: http://api.example.com/
  - with P4: https://api.example.com/
- getResourceUrl(): http://cdn.example.com... (unchanged).
- host[1] = 'https://api.example.com:80', later servers.live_api_server or ''. It is unused: no NetworkRequest or NetworkRequestGet call passes HOST=1, and its only other readers are the uncalled NetworkManager::Webview{News,DailyBonus,GachaBanner,Social}URL. No change is needed.
- If 'servers' is ever sent, it must be an object, e.g. {"live_api_server":"..."}, never an array or string.
- host[4] is reached only when /dls force=='1'; never send force=1.
- Keep public_host='api.example.com' with no port.

=== 3. tools/patch_apk.py --https ===
CLI:
  python3 -I tools/patch_apk.py --apk IN.apk --out OUT.apk --host api.example.com --https --root-ca pki/bfrevive-root-r1.pem [--no-purchase-https]
Rules:
- --https requires --root-ca.
- --host must equal the leaf SAN DNS name (at most 19 chars; today's host_patch validation applies).

Constants:
  PEM_OFFSET = 0x2318F2F
  PEM_SLOT_LEN = 0x546   # 1446 = 1445 + NUL
  PEM_MAX = 1445
  PEM_SLOT_SHA256 = 'cbfb7dcf86bc532d0f503479109faa03fcc68d6b98ef121252551d365b5b4605'
  GUARDS = [
    (0xF48CB4,  bytes.fromhex('809e009000bc3c9101008012'), 'BIO_new_mem_buf(0x2318f2f,-1)'),
    (0x2318F17, b'21BFCertificateProvider\0', '_ZTS before slot'),
    (0x23194D5, b'9PWWebView\0', '_ZTS after slot'),
    (0x2369CE3, b'https://\0', 'https literal used by P4'),
  ]
  PURCHASE_HTTPS_PATCHES = [  # P4, default ON in --https mode
    (0x1CE93D0, bytes.fromhex('e13100d0'), bytes.fromhex('01340090'), 'getPurchasePhpUrl adrp x1,0x2327000 -> adrp x1,0x2369000'),
    (0x1CE93D4, bytes.fromhex('21c00291'), bytes.fromhex('218c3391'), 'getPurchasePhpUrl add x1,#0xb0 -> add x1,#0xce3 ("https://")'),
  ]
  # Encodings verified with NDK clang/llvm-objdump. Do NOT modify the 'http://' literal at 0x23270B0:
  # getResourceUrl (CDN) uses it too.

Root validation (fail closed):
- Convert CRLF to LF and ensure a trailing LF.

inferred: SaveData::loadKeyChain at boot fills SaveData's user id (+0x18) from the keychain written on Confirm OK. After a successful transfer and relaunch, InitializeRequest therefore sends h7eY3sAK = the target id. That id matches only if the device's gumi user is now the target's gumi user, hence the device_key move.

Scene lifecycle: initialize() (loadLayout -> setLayoutControl) runs only after initConnect's request succeeds and checkConnectResult returns true. Evidence: TitleTransferCodeConfirmScene's layout draws ModelChangeUserInfo name and level, which only the Check reply fills, and the issue-done layout draws the AccountID from the Issue reply. Consequence: the Request scenes' local cleanup runs only on success.

Because the swap happens on Confirm OK, a failed TransferRequest leaves the keychain id = target while the device is still bound to its own gumi user. Initialize must ignore the mismatch and return the DB user for the authenticated gumi user (or '' for the new-user flow). On the title path a failed Transfer also routes to scene 866, an Option scene, out of context. So Transfer must succeed whenever Check succeeded: expiry grace, lock bypass on a correct password, and idempotent retries.

The old device keeps the target id in its keychain. After its token is cleared (SessionError -> Close) and it guest-logs-in to a new gumi user, a tolerant Initialize gives it user_id '' and the new-user flow.

On a fresh install the title-path transfer runs before the title tap, which is when TitleScene::touchBegan starts gumi login (GumiLiveScene ctor @0x1B88534 and observers @0x1B884DC). So iN7buP2h/iN7buP1i may be empty, unless loadKeyChain restores the gumi id and token that saveKeyChain stores.

4. CRYPTO (additions to gimuserver/utils/AccountSecurity.hpp; #include <cryptopp/pwdbased.h>)
- NewTransferCode(): 10 ASCII digits. The first digit is drawn from 1-9, the rest from 0-9, using AutoSeededRandomPool with rejection sampling (b < 250 for digits; b < 252 then b%9+1 for the first digit).
- NormalizeCode(s): trim ASCII whitespace; valid iff it matches ^[0-9]{10}$.
- CodeHash(c) = Sha256Hex("code:"+c).
- ValidNewPassword(p): ^[A-Za-z0-9]{4,12}$, byte-wise; this mirrors checkPassword @0x11D521C and the 4..12 count check.
- HashPassword(p, iter): 16-byte CSPRNG salt; CryptoPP::PKCS5_PBKDF2_HMAC<CryptoPP::SHA256>().DeriveKey(dk, 32, 0, (const byte*)p.data(), p.size(), salt, 16, iter, 0).
- VerifyPassword(p, enc): parse, re-derive with the stored iteration count, compare with account::ConstantTimeEquals.
- Unknown code: run one dummy derivation, so timing does not reveal whether the code exists.
- Run PBKDF2 off the IO loops: a dedicated trantor::EventLoopThread started once at app init, called via co_await drogon::queueInLoopCoro<std::string>(loop, [..]{...}).

 verifyCode(codeIn, pw, forTransfer):
   code = NormalizeCode(codeIn); if invalid -> dummy PBKDF2, M_BAD.
   row = SELECT ... WHERE code_hash = CodeHash(code); if none -> dummy PBKDF2, M_BAD.
   pwOk = VerifyPassword(pw, row.password_hash).
   If !forTransfer:
     locked_until > now -> M_LOCK.
     expires_at != 0 && now > expires_at -> M_EXP.
     !pwOk -> UPDATE failed_attempts = failed_attempts+1, locked_until = CASE WHEN failed_attempts+1 >= 10 THEN now+86400 ELSE locked_until END; return M_BAD.
     Otherwise UPDATE failed_attempts=0, last_check_ok_at=now; ok(row.user_id).
   If forTransfer:
     !pwOk -> same failure update; M_BAD (no lock bypass).
     pwOk -> ignore locked_until.
     Expiry: allow when expires_at == 0 || now <= expires_at + 900 || now - last_check_ok_at <= 900.

     UPDATE gumi_live_users SET device_key=NULL, token_hash=NULL, unbound_at=now WHERE id = s.gumiUserId;
